findings.reason: The protected source is already the conventional optimal rolling dynamic program: retain the cheapest valid prefix for each of three colors and compute all next states simultaneously from the prior row. The constant state, descriptive color names, and compact transitions are expert interview-quality, so no candidate is justified.

The app-local and immutable Accepted native sources have identical initial states, row unpacking, simultaneous color transitions, and final minimum; only collection typing syntax and the required LeetCode class-method wrapper differ.

The former 128/512-house tiers exceeded the source maximum of 100. Legal 4/20/100-house repeated-cost tiers now force every state transition. The current source passes at +0.00 relative exponent with a 1.04x largest runtime ratio; a correct implementation that recomputes every prefix passes every output and fails only scaling at +1.10 with a 44.62x ratio.

The Approach derives the three exhaustive predecessor transitions and induction argument, states the scalar $O(1)$ space bound, labels the single-house boundary, explains simultaneous assignment, and no longer treats empty input as source-legal.
The hash-bound Premium Reference remains verified against the source structure, preserving both factual examples, the first example's optimal coloring explanation, and all four constraints.

coverage: both source-fidelity-verified examples remain first as visible samples with exact matrices and minimum costs
the former empty matrix was removed because the verified source requires at least one house
single-house cases cover the legal minimum row count and both inclusive cost values 1 and 20
three consecutive rows sharing the same cheapest color expose the adjacency constraint and defeat independent row-wise greediness

a two-house matrix distinguishes simultaneous transitions from an incorrect sequential in-place state update
tied costs preserve multiple optimal prefixes, while a 100-row all-20 matrix reaches both the exact house-count and cost maxima
all eight expectations matched an independent top-down color-state oracle, and every case through ten houses also matched exhaustive coloring enumeration
5,000 seeded random legal matrices matched the independent oracle
the protected current source passed all eight correctness rows and all three unchanged benchmark tiers through the real-test engine; all benchmark outputs were correct and scaling passed
